To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The hChAT M-type promoter is activated in the presence of c-My and C/EBPB.
the c-My and the C/EBP family of transcription factors synergistically activate transcription of the human ChAT gene in neuronal cells.

the human choline-acetyltransferase gene is transcribed from multiple promoters, that the P2 promoter contains c-Myb- and C/EBPB-responsive elements, that the c-MyB and C/EBBP binding sites are located in close vicinity to each other and that the synergistic activation of the P2 promoter by c-MyB/C/EBP is mediated by CBP/p300.
In summary, our research is concerned with

transcriptional regulation of the human cholinergic phenotype and provides evidence that c-Myb, a transcription factor involved in hematopoiesis, also functions in the nervous system and that the synergistic activation of the ChAT gene by c- Myb and C/ EBP beta is mediated by a composite c- Myb / C/ EBP binding site and that CBP/p300 coactivators and the RAR/RXR/T3R complex are involved.
the identification of transcription factors that regulate the hChAT gene in neuronal and glial cell lines and the characterization of the mechanisms involved in this regulation.
the identification of the regulatory mechanisms involved in the transcriptional control of the hChAT gene in the context of neuronal differentiation and cell proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hChAT gene is a target for both c-Mybl and C/EBPs and that the c-Mybl/C/EBPbeta synergy is an important mechanism for ChAT gene transcriptional regulation in the neuronal system.

the hChAT gene is under transcriptional regulation by c-Mybl and C/EBPlbeta and that the synergistic activation of hChAT by c-Mybi and C/EBPi beta is dependent upon the presence of a composite element in the promoter region of the M-type promoter.

c-Myb, C/EBP, and NGFI-C (Egr4) are important transcriptional regulators of the hChAT gene in the neuronal system, and that the hChAT promoter M (P2)-type is the main one in the NG108-15 cells and the SN56 cell line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the c-Mybl/C/EBPbeta synergy is a general phenomenon and that the composite element is the key to the synergistic action of c-Mybl and C/EBPl.
the hChAT gene is regulated in a complex manner by c-Mybs, C/EBPb, NGFI-C and the nuclear receptors.
c-Myb, C/EBP and the coactivators are involved in the transcriptional regulation of the M-type ChAT gene in neuronal cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
c-Myb, C/EBP, NGFI-C and RAR/RXR/T3R are important transcriptional regulators of the human ChAT gene in neuronal and non-neuronal cell lines.
the synergistic action of c-Mybl and C/EBPs in the transcriptional activation of the hChAT gene is a general regulatory mechanism in both hematopoietic and neuronal cells.
a c-Mybc-Mybc-EBPbeta synergistic activation of the hChAT gene is a general mechanism for the regulation of neuronal gene expression.
